title: Design: Sales By Representative rows and dashes look as designed
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • You are signed in as a user with the "Admin" role at {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • The browser window is 1440 px wide with the zoom at 100%, and the design pictures "sbr-04-a4-sbr-c.png" (board 4.4) and "sbr-05-a4-sbr-expanded.png" (board 4.5) attached to this case are open beside it at 100% (actual size). Names, numbers and dates in the pictures are sample data.
  • Two active staff members at {Location-A} have their "Sales Representative" switch on: {Sales-rep-A} and {Sales-rep-B}.
    For example: {Sales-rep-A} is ZZAUTOTEST Ann Able and {Sales-rep-B} is ZZAUTOTEST Ben Able.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has no sales representative.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST SSR Fleet.
  • Today has one invoiced split work order (Labor {Sales-rep-A}, Parts {Sales-rep-B}), one invoiced work order with {Sales-rep-A} on both sides and one invoiced part sale with no shop supplies.
  • Starting screen: Reports > Sales By Representative is open for today in that browser window, with the Sales Type column off.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Compare the default report with the picture of board 4.4.
  2. Expand {Sales-rep-A}.
  3. Expand {Sales-rep-B} and compare with the picture of board 4.5.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: one row per representative; the filter reads "Sales Type: All"; no Sales Type column by default.
  • Step 2: {Sales-rep-A}'s invoice rows show.
  • Step 3: the split invoice shows under both representatives; a side a representative did not sell shows a dash (including Shop Supplies on the Parts row); the part sale with no shop supplies shows a dash under Shop Supplies and under Labor Delta, Labor Invoiced and Labor Margin.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Splitting Sales Representatives", Confluence 919928833, version 11 (21 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 22 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10890, story SV-11269 (Story 5, Credit each side on the invoice and in Sales By Representative), story SV-11272 (Story 8, Filter both sales reports by Sales Type)

  • S5-R15: “On a Labor row the parts columns show a dash, and on a Parts row the labor, hours and Shop Supplies columns show a dash, not $0.00. $0.00 is shown only for a real zero. A row that holds both sides, one person on both, keeps the report's rule that an invoice with no labor shows Labor Delta 0.0.”
  • S5-R15a: “On a Part Sales row, Shop Supplies shows the part sale's shop supplies, or a dash when the part sale has no shop supplies charge. $0.00 shows only when a shop supplies charge of $0.00 is on it.”
  • S5-R15b: “On a Part Sales row, Labor Delta, Labor Invoiced and Labor Margin, and the labor and hours cells of the Expanded downloads, show a dash on screen and in the PDF and are blank in the CSV. A part sale has no labor, so these columns don't apply to it.”
  • S5-R21: “The Sales Type column is off by default on screen, for every user.”
  • S8-R3: “With all three selected the filter reads "Sales Type: All". With none it reads "Sales Type: None". Otherwise it reads the selected names in option order, for example "Sales Type: Labor, Parts".”

From: Chris Ward's answers to the Splitting Sales Representatives question sheet (answers 1 to 38, 19 Oct 2026; answers 39 and 40, 21 Oct 2026), read 22 Oct 2026

  • Chris Ward's answer 24: “24. (a) as the feature spec: a dash on screen and in the PDF, an empty cell in the CSV. The 0.0 rule still applies to an invoice with one person on both sides.”
  • Chris Ward's answer 25: “25. (a) A dash when the part sale has no shop supplies; $0.00 only when it has a shop supplies line that totals $0.00. The design's $0.00 is a sample-data mistake.”
  • Chris Ward's answer 39: “39. (a) A dash on screen and in the PDF, and an empty cell in the CSV, as the design shows. A part sale has no labor, so the labor columns don't apply to it; it's the same rule as answers 24 and 25. This changes today's 0.00 / $0.00, so it's now listed under Release day. New S5-R15b, PRD v11.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Claude design canvas "Splitting Sales Representatives" (https://claude.ai/artifact/8MHqwyffAYtqZ6EccS5RUm), export read 19 Oct 2026, boards 4.4 One row per rep; 4.5 Expanded: Sales Type column off (the attached pictures are these boards).

Where the design and the PRD differ: The picture of board 4.5 shows $0.00 under Shop Supplies on the Parts row and on the part sales, while the board 4.5 note (quoted below) says a side a rep did not sell shows a dash. Chris Ward ruled on 19 Oct 2026 for the PRD's dash, and said the design's $0.00 on the part sales is a sample-data mistake (answers 24 and 25, quoted above); this case follows them.

Design pictures attached to this case: sbr-04-a4-sbr-c.png, sbr-05-a4-sbr-expanded.png.

  • Design — board 4.4 title: “4.4 One row per rep”
  • Design — board 4.4 note: “The filter is now "Sales Type". Devon 3 invoices, $1,314.68; Elliot 3 invoices, $2,788.81; total $4,103.49. A split invoice counts once for each rep who sold part of it; the totals do not change because of a split.”
  • Design — board 4.5 title: “4.5 Expanded: Sales Type column off”
  • Design — board 4.5 note: “Decision 40: the Sales Type column is off by default on screen. S1-12 appears under both reps: Devon with its parts, Elliot with its labor and shop supplies. A side a rep did not sell shows a dash.”
